import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.19

by F. B. Cannonito

Construct an explicit example of a finitely presented simple group with word
problem not solvable by a primitive recursive function.

By a theorem of Kuznetsov, every finitely presented simple group has solvable
word problem. The problem therefore asks for a finitely presented simple group
whose word problem, although decidable, is not decidable by a primitive
recursive function. The requirement that the example be "explicit" cannot be
expressed in Lean, so we formalise the existence of such a group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.19»

/--
Construct an explicit example of a finitely presented simple group with word
problem not solvable by a primitive recursive function.

We formalise this as an existence statement: there are $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and a
finite set of relators $R \subseteq F(x_1, \dots, x_n)$ such that the finitely
presented group $G = \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ is simple and the
word problem of $G$ is not primitive recursive. Here the word problem of $G$ is
the predicate on words $w$ in the letters $x_1^{\pm 1}, \dots, x_n^{\pm 1}$ that
holds exactly when $w = 1$ in $G$. Words are coded as lists of pairs
(generator, sign), i.e. as terms of `List (Fin n × Bool)`, for which Mathlib
provides a primitive recursive coding. Whether the word problem is primitive
recursive does not depend on the chosen finite presentation of $G$, nor on the
chosen primitive recursive coding of words.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.19» :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))), rels.Finite ∧
      IsSimpleGroup (PresentedGroup rels) ∧
      ¬ PrimrecPred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.19»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The decomposition table's single slot and its notes (existence Prop, PresentedGroup over Fin n with finite relators, IsSimpleGroup, non-Primrec characteristic function of the word problem under a primitive recursive coding of words) match the statement, and the file follows them.
modeling_decisions: 'Explicit example' is not expressible in Lean; per the decomposition table, the slot is formalized as a pure existence statement (documented in the module and theorem docstrings).

'Finitely presented simple group' is modeled as `PresentedGroup rels` with generator type `Fin n` and `rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))` with `rels.Finite`, rather than an abstract group `G` together with an isomorphism to such a presented group. This is equivalent since IsSimpleGroup is isomorphism-invariant and primitive recursiveness of the word problem is independent of the finite presentation chosen.

The word problem is taken over all words in the letters x_i^{±1}, coded as `List (Fin n × Bool)` (Mathlib's `FreeGroup.mk`; `(a, true)` = a, `(a, false)` = a⁻¹), using Mathlib's `Primcodable` instance for `List (Fin n × Bool)`, instead of over reduced words / a bespoke `Primcodable (FreeGroup (Fin n))` instance. The two are equivalent up to primitive recursive reductions (free reduction is primitive recursive).

'Not solvable by a primitive recursive function' is formalized as `¬ PrimrecPred (fun w => PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1)`, i.e. the characteristic function of the word problem is not primitive recursive. In the current Mathlib, `PrimrecPred p` is `∃ (_ : DecidablePred p), Primrec (fun a => decide (p a))`, so no classical decidability instance had to be introduced.
AMS tags 3 (mathematical logic and foundations / computability) and 20 (group theory) were chosen.

kourovka.«7.19».why: Stated as the existence Prop from the decomposition table: ∃ n and a finite set rels of relators in FreeGroup (Fin n) such that PresentedGroup rels is simple (IsSimpleGroup, hence nontrivial) and the word problem, i.e. the predicate w ↦ (PresentedGroup.mk rels (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1) on words w : List (Fin n × Bool), is not PrimrecPred (Mathlib's primitive recursive coding of lists of pairs). Existing primitives (PresentedGroup, IsSimpleGroup, FreeGroup.mk, PrimrecPred, Primcodable instances) suffice; no new definitions.

namespace Kourovka.«7.19»

Construct an explicit example of a finitely presented simple group whose word
problem is not solvable by a primitive recursive function.

The formal statement records the existence of finitely many generators and
finitely many relators with these properties. A word is a list of signed
generators in $\operatorname{Fin}(n) \times \operatorname{Bool}$, with its canonical
primitive-recursive coding, and is evaluated by the canonical maps from words
to the free group and then to the presented group.

    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      IsSimpleGroup (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) ∧
      ¬ PrimrecPred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        PresentedGroup.mk (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.19»
modeling_decisions: Formalized “construct an explicit example” as an existence proposition, since mathematical explicitness is not expressible as a Lean proposition.
Represented a finite presentation by `n : ℕ` generators indexed by `Fin n` and a `Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))` of relators, with the group concretely given by `PresentedGroup`.

Represented input words as `List (Fin n × Bool)` and evaluated them using `FreeGroup.mk` followed by `PresentedGroup.mk`; Mathlib's canonical `Primcodable` instances provide the required primitive-recursive coding of these words.

Used `¬ PrimrecPred` for the word-problem predicate. By definition this says that no primitive-recursive Boolean characteristic function decides whether a word represents the identity, without requiring a preselected decidable-equality algorithm for the quotient group.
Used `IsSimpleGroup`, whose Mathlib definition includes nontriviality.

by F. B. Cannonito

problem not solvable by a primitive recursive function.

By Kuznetsov's theorem the word problem of a finitely presented simple group is
always decidable, so the content of the problem is the failure of primitive
recursiveness. The requirement that the example be explicit cannot be expressed

problem not solvable by a primitive recursive function.

A finitely presented group is `PresentedGroup rels` for a finite set `rels` of
relators in the free group on finitely many generators $x_0, \dots, x_{n-1}$.
Its word problem is the set of words over the alphabet

A word is a list of pairs `(i, b)`, where `(i, true)` denotes $x_i$ and
`(i, false)` denotes $x_i^{-1}$, and `FreeGroup.mk` sends it to the free group.
The word problem is solvable by a primitive recursive function when it is a
`PrimrecPred` with respect to Mathlib's standard coding of `List (Fin n × Bool)`
by natural numbers; this does not depend on the finite presentation chosen.
-/

theorem kourovka.«7.19» :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      IsSimpleGroup (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) ∧
      ¬ PrimrecPred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        PresentedGroup.mk (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.19»

Finitely presented group modeled concretely as PresentedGroup (↑rels) with rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n)); every finitely presented group is isomorphic to one of this form, and simplicity and the (primitive-recursive) solvability of the word problem are invariant under isomorphism/change of finite presentation.

The one-word-equals-identity form of the word problem is used rather than the two-word equality form u = v; these are equivalent via the primitive recursive reduction (u, v) ↦ u v⁻¹.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 7.19

by F. B. Cannonito

Construct an explicit example of a finitely presented simple group with word
problem not solvable by a primitive recursive function.

A finitely presented group is given here as `PresentedGroup rels`, where the
generators are indexed by `Fin n` and `rels` is a finite set of relators in the
free group `FreeGroup (Fin n)`. Its word problem is the decision problem on words
$w \in$ `List (Fin n × Bool)` (letters are generators or their inverses) asking
whether the element of the group represented by $w$ is the identity. The word
problem is solvable by a primitive recursive function when the characteristic
function of this predicate, under Mathlib's primitive recursive coding of
`List (Fin n × Bool)` by natural numbers, is primitive recursive (`PrimrecPred`).

By a theorem of Kuznetsov, the word problem of a finitely presented simple group
is always decidable; the content of the problem is the failure of primitive
recursiveness. Whether the word problem is primitive recursive does not depend on
the chosen finite presentation, since a change of finite presentation is a
primitive recursive reduction. The word "explicit" cannot be captured formally, so
the formal statement is the existence of such a group.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«7.19»

/--
Construct an explicit example of a finitely presented simple group with word
problem not solvable by a primitive recursive function.

Formally: there exist $n$ and a finite set of relators $R \subseteq F(x_1, \dots, x_n)$
such that the group $G = \langle x_1, \dots, x_n \mid R \rangle$ is simple and the
characteristic function of its word problem
$w \mapsto [\,w =_G 1\,]$ on words $w$ in the letters $x_i^{\pm 1}$ is not primitive
recursive.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.19» :
    ∃ (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))),
      IsSimpleGroup (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))) ∧
      ¬ PrimrecPred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) =>
        PresentedGroup.mk (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1 := by
  sorry

/--
Kuznetsov's theorem: the word problem of a finitely presented (more generally,
recursively presented) simple group is decidable. Hence the content of
Problem 7.19 lies solely in the failure of primitive recursiveness.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 3 20]
theorem kourovka.«7.19».computablePred_wordProblem (n : ℕ) (rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n)))
    (h : IsSimpleGroup (PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))))) :
    ComputablePred fun w : List (Fin n × Bool) =>
      PresentedGroup.mk (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n))) (FreeGroup.mk w) = 1 := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«7.19»
attempts.decomposition_objections: None. The decomposition table's reading (existence of a finitely presented simple group whose word problem is not primitive recursive, with 'explicit' uncapturable) is the only faithful formal reading, and the file conforms to it.
modeling_decisions: Finite presentation is modeled as `PresentedGroup (rels : Set (FreeGroup (Fin n)))` with `rels : Finset (FreeGroup (Fin n))` (finitely many generators indexed by `Fin n`, finitely many relators).

Words are modeled as `List (Fin n × Bool)` (letters are generators with a sign bit) mapped to the group via `PresentedGroup.mk rels ∘ FreeGroup.mk`; this uses Mathlib's `Primcodable` instance for lists as the primitive recursive coding of words. Any other natural coding is primitive-recursively equivalent.

'Word problem not solvable by a primitive recursive function' is rendered as `¬ PrimrecPred (fun w => ⟦w⟧ = 1)`. `PrimrecPred` existentially quantifies the `DecidablePred` instance, so no classical decidability instance is needed and the choice of instance is immaterial.

The word problem is stated for the chosen presentation only; primitive recursiveness of the word problem is independent of the finite presentation (change of presentation is a primitive recursive reduction), as noted in the decomposition table.

The statement is not a yes/no question ('Construct an explicit example ...'), so the plain existence form `theorem … : ∃ … := by sorry` is used rather than `answer(sorry) ↔ …`, following CONTRIBUTING.md. The word 'explicit' cannot be captured in Lean; this is recorded in the docstrings.

An additional `@[category research solved]` declaration `kourovka.«7.19».computablePred_wordProblem` states Kuznetsov's theorem (word problem of a finitely presented simple group is decidable, `ComputablePred`) as context showing that the problem's content is exclusively the failure of primitive recursiveness. It is not a slot and may be dropped if the reviewer prefers a single declaration.

All primitives (PresentedGroup, IsSimpleGroup, FreeGroup.mk, PrimrecPred, Primcodable instances for List/Prod/Fin/Bool) exist in Mathlib. 'Explicit' is not formalizable and is noted in the docstring.
